**Theme:** OpenAI launches GPT-5.6 three-tier family, Anthropic Fable 5 export controls lifted with new government compliance terms, Abbott reverses to call for rural Texas data center ban, nearly a third of Indiana counties restrict data centers, Section 48E ITC hard deadline passed July 4.

## Data Science & Analytics
- OpenAI GPT-5.6 family: Sol ($5/$30/1M tokens, Cerebras 750 tok/sec, Terminal-Bench SOTA), Terra ($2.50/$15), Luna ($1/$6). Partner preview rollout, not yet public. Cache breakpoints + 30-min min cache life.
- Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5 launched June 30: most agentic Sonnet, near Opus 4.8 performance. Intro pricing $2/$10 per 1M tokens through Aug 31, then $3/$15. Self-checking without prompting.
- Meta 8,000 layoffs + 7,000 reassigned to AI teams (Applied AI Engineering, Agent Transformation Accelerator XFN). Zuckerberg memo: acknowledged "mistakes." 154,000 total tech layoffs in 2026.

## AI in Practice
- Fable 5 + Mythos 5 export controls lifted June 30 by Commerce Department. Terms: proactive security detection, government standards coordination for upcoming models, malicious-use reporting. 18-day ban, original rationale never publicly stated. Commerce Secretary Lutnick announced.
- 80% of enterprise data team effort still goes to data prep not insight. Deloitte: 72% have production AI, 60% lack governance; governance → 12× more projects reach production. Nearly half of 800 leaders say AI projects haven't met expectations (despite $1M+ annual investment).

## Energy Buildout & Infrastructure
- Section 48E ITC deadline passed July 4. Projects starting after July 4: no ITC if not in service by Dec 31, 2027. Pre-deadline projects: 30% ITC through Dec 31, 2027 (4-yr continuity safe harbor). OBBBA provision. Foreign Entity of Concern: 40% component limit for Chinese/Russian/Iranian/NK sources.
- Google closed $4.75B Intersect Power acquisition (deal announced Dec 2025, closed H1 2026). 10.8 GW clean energy by late 2028. Used 500 MW BTM solar + 2 GWh BESS to bypass 5-yr PJM queue — 18-month construction-to-operation. First hyperscaler to own renewable developer.
- EIA: renewables hit 30% of U.S. electricity as of June 2026. 86 GW new 2026 capacity: 51% solar, 28% battery storage, 14% wind. NC House passed Ratepayer Protection Act 69-44: requires Duke Energy nuclear certification before coal retirement; bans local DC incentives ≥100 MW; mandates 15-yr contracts with ratepayer protections. Now in NC Senate.

## Rural Development Opportunities
- Abbott called June 30 for outright ban on data centers in rural Texas neighborhoods + eliminate tax breaks. Reversal from "epicenter of AI" (Nov 2025). Earlier June directive (PUC/ERCOT, infrastructure self-funding) still in effect. TX legislature doesn't convene until Jan 2027. PUC/ERCOT joint memo due July 17.
- Indiana: IU Environmental Resilience Institute — 11 counties with ordinances, 17 with moratoriums, 2 (Marshall and Cass) with outright bans as of July 6. Meta's $10B Lebanon campus was the magnet. State government is still actively courting DCs; legislature has not acted.
- NY: Hochul still deliberating, has until end of year; 10 days once bill formally delivered. Has said siting belongs at municipal level.
- NC: 29 of 100 counties with moratoriums or about to. Elon University poll: 44% oppose vs 24% support DC in community. Plurality opposition across all demographics.

## Cross-Sector Signals
- July 4 ITC deadline + Abbott rural ban call arrived same week — two policy moves compressing rural Texas energy-plus-DC build window from different directions.
- Fable 5 settlement creates bilateral AI safety compact with no legislative framework — de facto precedent for Commerce to impose compliance on frontier labs without rulemaking.
- Inference cost race (Sonnet 5 at $2/1M, Luna at $1/1M) moving opposite direction from DC build-out demand projections — no regulatory study has yet incorporated the efficiency curves into demand forecasts.

- **People:** Howard Lutnick (Commerce Secretary), Mark Zuckerberg (Meta CEO), Greg Abbott (TX Gov), Kathy Hochul (NY Gov)
- **Places:** Indiana (Marshall County/Cass County/Lebanon/Boone County), Texas (rural areas/East Texas), North Carolina (Stokes County), New York (statewide moratorium pending)
- **Capital figures:** $4.75B Google-Intersect, $5/$30 per 1M Sol tokens, $2/$10 Sonnet 5, 30% U.S. electricity from renewables, 86 GW 2026 capacity additions, 10.8 GW Google clean energy, 11 counties/17 moratoriums/2 bans Indiana, 29 of 100 NC counties

**Theme:** Prediction markets cool on GPT-5.6, a national poll finds bipartisan support for data center moratoriums, and the Woodbury County vote lands — with a jurisdictional hole.

## Data Science & Analytics
- GPT-5.6 Polymarket odds collapsed: 83% → 18% for June 22-28 window. $1.1M volume. OpenAI confirms nothing. ChatGPT Pro users report longer responses and hour-plus generation times suggesting internal testing.
- Anthropic Claude Corps: $150M fellowship, 1,000 fellows placed in nonprofits for 12-month paid deployments ($85K/yr). First cohort of 100 starts October 2026. Applications close July 17.
- Domino Data Lab: Gartner MQ Visionary 3rd consecutive year (19 vendors evaluated). 4.6/5.0 Peer Insights rating.

## AI in Practice
- Stanford AI Index 2026: 62% cite security as #1 barrier to scaling agentic AI (vs 38% technical, 38% regulatory). 65% of enterprises with deployed agents experienced confirmed security incident. 63% cannot enforce purpose limitations; 60% cannot terminate misbehaving agents.
- Foxconn MoMClaw on NVIDIA FOX blueprint: multi-agent manufacturing system on DGX Station (GB300). Claims 80% faster root-cause analysis, 15% labor productivity gains, 10% lower equipment failure rates. Vendor-reported metrics.
- Enterprise AI reality check: 80% of effort in data prep; 43% cite data quality as top obstacle; 79% face adoption challenges despite $1M+ annual investment (Writer); fewer than 10% scaled agents beyond pilot; nearly half of 800 leaders say AI projects haven't met expectations (Coastal).

## Energy Buildout & Infrastructure
- GOP senator introduced bill placing DC grid connections under federal FERC oversight. Joins Power for the People Act (Van Hollen, cost-shifting) and DATA Act (Cotton, FERC exemption for self-powered DCs). Three competing federal frameworks.
- Deep Atomic proposed first nuclear-powered AI DC campus at Idaho National Laboratory. MK60 SMR: 60 MW electric, 60 MW cooling, 200 MW thermal. Consortium: Clayco, Paragon, EvapCo. Phase 1 uses grid/geothermal/solar while reactor builds (24-36 months).
- Texas overtook Northern Virginia as top global DC market. NVIDIA-IREN 5 GW partnership, Sweetwater TX 2 GW flagship. Campuses routinely demand 100 MW+.

## Rural Development Opportunities
- Woodbury County IA passed 12-month moratorium 5-0 (June 23). Covers unincorporated areas only. The 900-acre Salix annexation site (MidAmerican Energy-linked) sits inside city limits — exempt. Jurisdictional gap.
- Data for Progress national poll (June 23): 63% of likely voters support pausing DC construction 1+ year. Bipartisan: 67% Dem, 66% Ind, 58% Rep. N=1,090, MOE ±3 pts.
- Rolla MO council voted unanimously (June 24) to draft DC moratorium. Preemptive — no proposals received. Followed Governor's Forum on AI/DCs at Missouri S&T (June 18).
- USDA deadlines: Community Connect $17M (June 29), DLT $27M (June 30), REDLG (June 30). REAP frozen.

## Cross-Sector Signals
- Moratorium politics going national: 63% poll support, bipartisan; Woodbury jurisdictional gap; Rolla preemptive. Expect moratorium language in 2026 midterms.
- Security is the bottleneck: Stanford 62%, Gartner 60% abandonment, Writer 79% challenges. Governance platforms may be next capital allocation shift.
- Three competing federal DC grid frameworks live: more FERC control vs. cost-shifting protection vs. FERC exemption. Section 206 responses in August will shape which gains traction.

## AI in Practice

- NVIDIA liquid cooling reference design at London Climate Week (June 22): 45°C closed-loop coolant, claims 100% water reduction at server level. Caveats: addresses ~25-33% of total facility water footprint (TechCrunch); supplemental cooling needed above 115°F.
- HarnessX framework (arXiv, June 2026): 10-layer self-improving harness stack raises Terminal-Bench pass rates 50%+ with fixed base weights. Perplexity Search as Code: 85% token reduction. Inference scaffolding becoming competitively important.

## Energy Buildout & Infrastructure
- Gartner (June 10): global DC electricity 565 TWh in 2026 (+26% YoY), 132 GW power demand (+27%). AI servers = 31% of DC power; will surpass conventional servers by 2027.
- EIA: record 86 GW U.S. generation capacity planned for 2026 — solar 43.4 GW (51%), battery 24 GW (28%), wind 11.8 GW (14%), gas 6.3 GW. Vineyard Wind 1 (800 MW), Revolution Wind (715 MW), SunZia (3,650 MW) targeting 2026.
- Seattle data center moratorium (June 9): largest U.S. city to pass one. Unanimous. 369 MW proposed on ~1 GW grid. One-year ban on facilities >20 MVA.

## Rural Development Opportunities
- Woodbury County IA votes today (June 23) on 1-year moratorium. All 5 supervisors support. Triggered by Salix 900-acre annexation for potential DC; MidAmerican Energy confirmed. Jurisdiction gap: DC may be inside city limits.
- Skagit County WA: 6-month preemptive moratorium (June 1) on rural DCs >2 MW / 2,000 sq ft. No proposals received. Protecting farmland/water. Public hearing July 14.
- Fort Payne AL: unanimous 6-month moratorium, preemptive — no DC proposals. Homewood and Cullman AL also debating. Movement arrives in pro-development state.
- USDA deadlines: Community Connect $17M (June 29), DLT $27M (June 30). REAP frozen. REDLG June 30.

## Cross-Sector Signals
- Moratorium movement gone urban + West Coast: Seattle (largest city), Skagit County WA, plus preemptive moratoriums in towns with no proposals. 15 states involved.
- Supply constraints stacking: 132 GW demand vs 30-50% pipeline slippage vs 86 GW generation additions facing queue delays.
- Open-source models gain ground as export controls fragment access: GLM-5.2 frontier-adjacent under MIT while Fable/Mythos restricted.

- Moratorium geography expanding west (Reno NV, Larimer CO). 14 states now considered or enacted DC moratoriums. Woodbury County vote tomorrow tests Iowa formalization.
- SMR pipeline broadening beyond existing nuclear sites. Elementl Power Ohio = greenfield build. Four distinct SMR deployment models now in play.
- Inference efficiency gains (Gemini 3.5 Flash 40% cheaper, harness engineering +50% gains) may moderate but not reverse DC power demand. BNEF 106 GW assumes current efficiency trends.

**Theme:** FERC fires its biggest shot at grid bottlenecks; Iowa joins the moratorium wave; GM bets sodium-ion can power the data center buildout.

## Data Science & Analytics

- Alteryx unveils Agent Studio and MCP Server at Inspire 2026 — analysts can convert workflows to autonomous agents. MCP protocol adoption widens beyond dev tools.

## Energy Buildout & Infrastructure
- FERC issued landmark Section 206 show-cause orders (June 18) to all six RTOs/ISOs: justify or rewrite large-load interconnection tariffs within 60 days. 30-day reliability report required. Covers 200M Americans, 30+ states. Most aggressive federal grid-connection action yet.
- FERC approved PJM expedited interconnection track (June 9): 10 projects/year, 250 MW min, 3-year commercial deadline. $500K study deposit + $15K/MW readiness deposit. 100% network upgrade costs on applicant. Expires end 2027.
- SC PSC approved Dominion-Santee Cooper $5B, 2,180 MW Canadys gas plant (June 12). Colleton County. Environmental groups flagged Edisto River siting.
- GM-Peak Energy partnership (June 9): GM manufactures sodium-ion cells in Michigan; Peak integrates into passively cooled storage (20% cost cut vs lithium-ion, 99%+ uptime). Trial production 2028. Targets utilities and DCs.
- Behind-the-meter DC gas plants escape state rate regulation, may raise bills more than grid connection. PJM proposed 50 MW BTM netting threshold (Feb). White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge (March) is nonbinding.

## Rural Development Opportunities
- Woodbury County IA: all five supervisors support one-year DC moratorium (June 17). MidAmerican Energy confirmed DC under consideration on 900 acres Salix annexed April. Vote expected June 23. Iowa is 10th state with active moratorium efforts.
- NY data center moratorium awaits Hochul. Passed June 5 (Senate 44-16, Assembly 102-39). Industry lobbying for veto. Hochul has expressed reservations. 10-day clock starts on delivery.
- USDA broadband grants: Community Connect ($17M, deadline June 29) and DLT ($27M, deadline June 30). REAP grants frozen. REDLG deadline June 30.
- Champlain Hudson Power Express: 1,250 MW HVDC from Quebec to NYC hit commercial operation May 13 (early). 10.4 TWh/yr, $97.50/MWh (yr 1), 25-year contract. 339 miles, longest buried line in North America. 20% of NYC power.

## Cross-Sector Signals
- FERC Section 206 orders force all RTOs to confront large-load interconnection simultaneously. If costs shift to DCs, rural self-generation sites gain advantage — but behind-the-meter gas loophole compounds ratepayer problem.
- Moratorium movement: Iowa = 10th state. Jurisdiction contests continue (Woodbury mirrors Hood County TX pattern). Hochul decision will set national precedent.
- Sodium-ion storage (GM-Peak Energy) converges with gas plant cost spiral. If 20% cost reduction materializes at scale by 2028–29, offers domestic non-lithium alternative as gas turbine slots sold out into next decade.

**1. Moratorium movement acquires national political weight**

What started as county-level zoning votes crossed into organized political force this week. The Data for Progress national poll (June 23, N=1,090) showed 63% of likely voters support a one-year pause on data center construction — 67% Democrats, 66% Independents, 58% Republicans. The Woodbury County IA vote (5-0, June 23) demonstrated both the movement's momentum and its structural weakness: the county's moratorium covers only unincorporated areas, while the 900-acre Salix annexation site — linked to MidAmerican Energy — sits inside city limits and is fully exempt. Rolla MO voted unanimously to draft a preemptive moratorium (June 24) with zero proposals on the table. Alabama produced a cluster: Fort Payne, Homewood, Cullman, Morgan County, and Jefferson County (vote pending). Missouri's House Special Committee on Intergovernmental Affairs scheduled a formal regulatory hearing for September 16. That's the first state legislative body to convene explicitly in response to the wave.

**Watch next week:** Jefferson County AL vote outcome. Hochul NY decision remains the highest-stakes pending action — industry lobbying for veto is intensifying.

Applicants must submit to distribution and transmission service providers by July 10. ERCOT classifies projects in August; the final transmission plan is not expected until Fall 2027. Data centers must fund their own interconnection costs, and 80% of posted security is forfeited if a project withdraws or misses a milestone by six months.

This is the first concrete regulatory mechanism to flow from the governor-level executive action narrative. Texas has simultaneously overtaken Northern Virginia as the top global data center market, anchored by the NVIDIA-IREN 5-gigawatt partnership and the Sweetwater flagship campus.
